**KJAK03*** is a medical procedure code designating laparotomy and peritoneal lavage. Within the context of Danish healthcare quality development, it serves as a critical identifier for tracking specific acute surgical interventions.

The code is significant for its formal inclusion in the population definition of the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (Acute Surgery Database) [^src1]. According to the 2024 AKDB report, the database's population formation was expanded to include KJAK03*—alongside codes KJAK01* and KJAK04*—to ensure complete and accurate coverage of relevant acute surgical procedures [^src1]. This methodological adjustment was necessary because these specific procedures are actively used in the treatment of relevant patients at certain hospitals, and their prior omission risked incomplete data capture [^src1].

This technical change is part of a broader narrative in the 2024 report focusing on methodological adjustments, supplementary analyses, and the critical discussion of quality indicators (such as antibiotic timing and 90-day mortality). By refining the underlying data sources and population definitions with codes like KJAK03*, organizations like Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut and LKT Akutkirurgi aim to improve treatment standards and ensure robust, standardized tracking of acute surgical care across Denmark [^src1].
